_machine_notes: AMD EPYC 9354P -- 1 socket, 32 cores / 64 threads, BIOS in NPS4 so the
socket presents 4 numa nodes of 16 cpus and ~47 GiB each (~187 GiB total).
L3 is 8 x 32 MiB (one per CCD); L2 is 1 MiB per core, i.e. 512 KiB per
hyperthread when both siblings run -- that is what get_optimal_radix()
Keys beginning with '_' are comments and are ignored by run_join.py.
_data_dir: All output for this spec lives under <data_dir>/, relative to run_join.py:
Change 'tag'/'data_dir' together after a BIOS change (e.g. NPS1) so the
two collections do not clobber each other.
_defaults: Applied to every run, then overridden by that run's own 'args'.
relation_r_size / relation_s_size are counts of 16-byte tuples:
The skew sweep uses these sizes (r = 1 GB, s = 15 GB); the relation_size
sweep overwrites both with the swept value (r = s).
_params: Swept x-axes. A run may override a list under its own 'params' key;
an empty list there means 'skip this sweep for this run'.
ht-fill and radix are derived per point, not listed here:
mode 13 -> ht-fill = ceil(r*100/(r+s)), capped by the run's max_ht_fill
mode 16 -> radix   = get_optimal_radix(r, ht-fill) against L2 above
_runs: Every run is self-describing: its 'args' carry the numa policy, so
run_join.py derives the hugepage plan from them and nothing else.
threads split evenly over the 4 nodes; global ht MPOL_INTERLEAVE'd
over all of them; relation and radix arenas follow first touch, so
they land on whichever node their own thread runs on.
arena.mem_bind(np_mem_node_msk) only when numa_split == 10, which with more
than one bit set INTERLEAVES the per-thread radix partitions instead of
leaving them thread-local first-touch. Split 1 keeps radix's partitions
node-local, which is the property the join is supposed to have. Use split 10
with masks only for a node *subset* (there is no other way to select one),
and remember radix is then a different experiment.
Footprint at these sizes is ~40 GiB (16 relations + 16 table + 8
g_zipf_values), i.e. ~10 GiB of hugepages per node plus the g_zipf_values
vector. That fits the 4-node config comfortably but not a single 47 GiB
node -- which is why only n4 is collected here. Run with --dry-run to see
the exact per-node budget before committing.

_cmake_flags: CAS_PREFETCHW=ON is deliberate and should stay on. It defaults to OFF in
CMakeLists.txt, which makes cas's insert prefetch a read-only prefetcht0, so
every CAS pays an S->E coherence upgrade. Turning it on takes cas's build
phase from 167 to 124 cyc/op on this box and makes it beat cas23 (130)
instead of losing to it by 1.28x. cas23 is unaffected -- it always
prefetches for write. Probe is unchanged either way.
_reps: Every sweep point is measured 5 times and all samples are kept.
throughput_mops holds the per-point median; throughput_samples (and the
probe/build cyc_per_op sample lists) hold the raw runs. plot_data.py draws
the median with a min/max band. This matters because cas's run-to-run
spread is ~5 cyc/op on probe (sd 4-6% of mean) while cas23's is ~2, so
single-run points cannot resolve the ~10% gaps this tree is measuring.
